headline: Approved consent agenda orders, passed two ordinances, postponed a legislative committee ordinance, and approved four special amusement licenses.
summary: Residents spoke during public comment about homelessness, ICE actions, a vacant property ordinance, and concerns about the Ethics Board. The Council passed the June 22, 2026 minutes and nine consent agenda items including property deeds, grants, and a lease. It postponed Ordinance 26-222 to July 27, 2026, passed Ordinance 26-223 and Resolves 26-224 and 26-225, and approved special amusement licenses for four businesses after public hearings.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 22, 2026 regular meeting.
Passed Order 26-228 authorizing a municipal quitclaim deed for real estate at 177 Larkin Street.
Passed Order 26-229 authorizing a municipal quitclaim deed for real estate at 187 Laurel Circle.
Passed Order 26-230 authorizing the City Manager to accept $6,440 in funds from a state criminal forfeiture.
Passed Order 26-231 authorizing a lease agreement with Varney Aviation, LLC for Building #457 at Bangor International Airport.
Passed Order 26-232 authorizing the sale of property at 45 Allen Street to Rent 207 Properties, LLC for $60,000.
Passed Order 26-233 authorizing the sale of property at 299 Essex Street to Tong Lu for $35,000.
Passed Order 26-234 authorizing a lease agreement with Bangor Nursing and Rehabilitation Center for office and clinic space for Bangor Public Health.
Passed Resolve 26-235 ratifying staff action to apply for up to $30,000 from the John T. Gorman Foundation Direct Service Grant Program.
Passed Resolve 26-236 accepting and appropriating $1,869,733 from the Maine Department of Health and Human Services for the Maine Prevention Network for fiscal years 2027 and 2028.
Gave first reading to Ordinance 26-237 amending Chapter 33, Code of Ethics.
Postponed Ordinance 26-222 amending the duties of the Legislative Committee to the July 27, 2026 City Council meeting, by a 9-0 vote.
Passed Ordinance 26-223 amending Chapter 165, Land Development Code, to add flexibility for manufactured home parks existing as of January 1, 2026, by a 9-0 vote.
Passed Resolve 26-224 accepting and appropriating a $10,000 Housing Opportunity Program Municipal Ordinance Development Grant from the Maine Office of Community Affairs.
Passed Resolve 26-225 accepting and appropriating $1,144,879 in HUD grant funds for the Bangor Rental Assistance Program.
Approved the Special Amusement License for Bangor Grande Aviators, LLC d/b/a Blue Sky Lounge, 357 Odlin Road, after a public hearing.
Approved the Special Amusement License for Waterfront Concerts, LLC d/b/a Waterfront Concerts, 1 Railroad Street, after a public hearing.
Approved the Special Amusement License for Roca Azul LLC d/b/a Roca Azul Mexican Restaurant, 248 Odlin Road, after a public hearing.
Approved the Special Amusement License for Seadog Ventures, Inc. d/b/a Seadog Ventures, Inc., 26 Front Street, after a public hearing.

# MINUTES OF REGULAR MEETING BANGOR CITY COUNCIL – JULY 13, 2026

Meeting called to order at 7:00 PM
Chaired by Council Chair Hawes
Councilors Absent: None
Meeting adjourned at 8:35 PM

**PUBLIC COMMENT**

Amber Webb, Joyce Mallery, Tyler Shanahan, Marlene Brochu, Charlie Longo, Jeremy Russell, and Richard Chaucer spoke regarding homelessness.

Scott Pardy expressed his opinion on the Council's performance and felt very little was being accomplished.

Philip Henry had serious concerns as to where tax money was going and whether certain Councilors were recusing from discussions in which they may have a conflict.

Michael Furow felt the Chair of the Ethics Board acted like a dictator and there was an appearance of unethical standards with two board members.

Zoe Smith spoke against the federal government's administration.

Grace Nichols, Teal Vasquez and Adam Baker expressed their concerns regarding ICE and the need to condemn their actions in Biddeford.

Abbigail Short and Jody McDonald expressed their disappointment that the Council did not pass Order 26-095.

Emily Ellis and Hal Wheeler spoke regarding the vacant and abandoned property ordinance and the need for it to be applied and enforced equally.

Hilari Simmons and Suzette Furrow's written comments are attached.

Good evening, Mayor, Councilors, and members of the public.

Thank you for the opportunity to speak this evening.

I am here because I believe the public deserves confidence that the City's Code of Ethics is applied fairly, consistently, and without regard to who the individual is or what position they hold.

Ethics standards exist to protect the integrity of government. They are intended to ensure that public officials conduct themselves in a manner that promotes transparency, impartiality, and public trust. Those standards only have value if they are enforced equally.

My questions tonight concern consistency.

When City Councilors give interviews to the Bangor Daily News or other media outlets on matters involving City business, under what circumstances are they considered to be speaking on behalf of the City versus expressing their personal opinions?

For example, Councilors Michael Beck and Susan Faloon have participated in media interviews while serving on the Council. What policy governs those communications? Are councilors authorized to speak on behalf of the City, or are those interviews considered personal commentary? If there is a distinction, how is it determined, and is that standard applied uniformly to every member of the Council?

I have the same question regarding social media.

Many elected officials maintain Facebook pages or other public social media accounts that identify them as City Councilors and regularly discuss City issues. When those pages are used to communicate with the public about City business, does the City consider those communications to be official, personal, or a combination of both? Has the Council adopted any guidance or standards governing the use of social media by elected officials?

I also have questions regarding conflicts of interest in the ethics process itself.

What measures are in place to ensure that members of boards or committees responsible for reviewing ethics complaints are free from actual or perceived conflicts of interest? Are members required to disclose relationships, affiliations, or other circumstances that could affect—or appear to affect—their impartiality? When appropriate, are recusals required to preserve the integrity of the process?

Transparency is essential to maintaining public confidence. Residents should be able to trust that ethics decisions are based solely on the facts, the City's Code of Ethics, and a fair, impartial review—not on personalities, political viewpoints, or personal relationships.

Finally, I ask the Council to consider whether the same expectations are being applied to every elected official. Equal treatment under the City's ethics policies is fundamental to good government. If one official is held accountable for certain conduct, the public should understand how similar situations involving other officials are evaluated and why the outcomes may differ.

These questions are not intended to criticize any individual. They are intended to promote transparency, consistency, and accountability in the application of the City's ethics standards.

The people of Bangor deserve confidence that their government operates fairly, that ethical standards are applied equally, and that every public official is held to the same expectations.

Thank you for your time and your consideration.

Monday, July 13, 2026

My name is Suzette Furrow, I am a resident of Bangor.
The opinions I express are my own and do not reflect those of any committee I may be a member of.

I would like to talk about the City of Bangor Ethics Board. I attended the Ethics Board meeting on June 30, 2026. I spoke during the public comment time. I spoke about the chair of the Ethics Board. The chair is a business partner with one of the members of the Ethics Board. According to the Board of Ethics Procedural Rules Article IV-Due Process and Ethics SS4.2 Public Meetings:

"Board Members may not discuss pending matters with each other outside of a Board meeting. No decision may be made by the Board outside of a regular or special meeting of the Board. Board members may discuss pending matters with City Staff or their representative(s)."

Whether or not the chair or the Board member discuss pending matters is irrelevant. The fact that they work together (run a business together) should not be allowed. The chair as the leader of the Board, should not have a business relationship (partnership) with one of its members. I cannot think of any other Board or Committee representing the City of Bangor that has a chair who has a business partnership with one of its members. Of all Boards and committees, the Ethics Board should be held to a higher standard.

Also, according to the Board of Ethics Procedural Rules under Article VII-Administrative Provisions, SS7.3 Procedural Rules:

"The rules contained in the current edition of **Democratic Rules of Order** shall govern the Board in all cases to which they are applicable and in which they are not inconsistent with State law, City ordinance, these procedures and any rules adopted by this Board."

According to the **Democratic Rules of Order**, during Formal meetings: **the chair guides impartially and does not participate in discussion. The chair's function is to maintain order, recognize speakers, and ensure procedures are followed.**

I would urge the Bangor City Council and the legal department to review the Ethics Board meeting which took place on June 30, 2026, and consider the fact that the chair is supposed to follow the **Democratic Rules of Order** and not participate in discussion as well as the fact that the chair is in business with one of the members of the Ethics Board.

Also, the Bangor City Council and the Legal Department should consider that 3 members are required for a quorum for the Ethics Board. This means that 2 of the three members for a quorum could be the 2 that are in business together.

Before the City Council considers imposing punishments based on findings from the Ethics Board, I suggest the Council examine the Ethics Board and whether they are following their own Procedural Rules and **the Democratic Rules of Order** which their Board is supposed to adhere to.

Thank you
